mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over 3 consecutive months indicates the Federal Reserve is shifting from tightening to easing, lowering discount rates and increasing equity present value, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day forward returns despite a sustained FEDFUNDS decline, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% triggers a risk-off reaction in equity markets, compressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate higher borrowing costs and reduced corporate leverage.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day forward returns in this regime, or Rank IC > 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) above 200,000 indicates a strengthening labor market, prompting optimism about corporate hiring and productivity, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day forward returns despite a sustained PAYEMS rise, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
